item.text: I’m re-reading the current tree with a focus on the next genuine design improvement. The main remaining awkwardness is that insertion success is inferred indirectly from `size`, and the traversal enum still depends on tree internals to execute its policy.

I’m making two deeper structural changes now. First, insertion will carry explicit mutation state instead of inferring success from `size`; second, traversal behavior will live directly on each enum constant instead of being encoded as visit-step data.

One follow-up edit is needed before verification: the traversal enum’s abstract method should be package-visible so the constant bodies can override it correctly. After that I’ll compile and run the demo.
The refactor is in place. I’m compiling and running it now to confirm the explicit insertion state and enum-owned traversal both preserved behavior.
The behavior stayed stable. I’m pulling final line references so the summary can point to the insertion and traversal design changes directly.

Further refactored [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:8) in two places.

Traversal behavior now lives directly on each `TraversalOrder` constant instead of being encoded as step data and interpreted elsewhere. Each order owns its recursive implementation at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:8), and `forEach(...)` just delegates to that policy at [AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:130). That removes the extra visit-step abstraction and keeps traversal semantics with the enum that defines them.

I also replaced the indirect “compare `size` before and after” insertion result with explicit mutation state. `insert(T)` now uses `InsertionState` ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:81)) and the recursive insert marks success at the actual insertion point ([AVLTree.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/044_avl_tree_insertion/AVLTree.java:166)). That makes the return value semantics clearer without reintroducing a recursive transport object.

Verification: `javac AVLTree.java AVLTreeDemo.java` succeeded, and `java AVLTreeDemo` still prints `30 20 10 25 40 50`.
